citations.short: Late submission of annual safety reports
citations.long: Not all annual periodic adverse drug experience reports have been submitted within 60 days of the anniversary date of the approval of the application.

citations.short: Late submission of quarterly safety reports

An annual report was not submitted within 60 days of the anniversary date of U.S. approval of the application to the FDA division responsible for reviewing the application.

citations.short: Defined areas of adequate size for operations
citations.long: The separate or defined areas and control systems necessary to prevent contamination or mix-ups are deficient.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Drug products do not bear an expiration date determined by appropriate stability data to assure they meet applicable standards of identity, strength, quality and purity at the time of use.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed

Employees are not given training in the particular operations they perform as part of their function.

citations.long: The separate or defined areas and control systems necessary to prevent contamination or mix-ups are deficient.
Written procedures are not established and followed for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment, including utensils, used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of a drug product.
Deviations from written production and process control procedures are not recorded and justified.
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Procedures for the preparation of master production and control records are not described in a written procedure.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications.
Procedures describing the handling of written and oral complaints related to drug products are deficiently written or followed.
Complaint records are deficient in that they do not include the findings of the investigation and follow-up.
